title: Triviality of phi-four theory and the Higgs sector's consistency
bottleneck: Rigorous renormalization-group arguments suggest that four-dimensional phi-four theory is 'trivial,' meaning its continuum limit is a free theory with vanishing interactions, which would make the Higgs self-interaction inconsistent at arbitrarily high energies. Lattice evidence supports triviality, implying the Standard Model needs new physics before the Landau pole.
why_it_blocks: If the Higgs sector cannot be fundamental up to the Planck scale, the Standard Model is provably an effective theory and the scale of its breakdown becomes a concrete target for experiment.
current_state: The triviality bound places the Standard Model's cutoff comfortably above LHC energies for a 125 GeV Higgs, so the issue is one of principle rather than urgency, but it remains mathematically unresolved.
